content.title: About
content.content: Potato chips, popped, NFS are light, crunchy snacks made by puffing thinly sliced potatoes without added oil. They have a delicate texture, a classic potato flavor, and lower fat content compared with traditional fried chips.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Puffing works by rapid moisture evaporation, creating a porous structure without the need for oil frying.
The NFS (National Food Service) brand is known for products aimed at corporate catering and bulk foodservice.
Popped chips are often featured in diet menus because they contain fewer calories than regular fried chips.
A wide range of flavors is available: classic salted, cheese, barbecue, and spicy chili.
The puffing process helps retain more vitamin C, which is usually lost during deep‑frying.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Because no oil is used during production, popped chips contain significantly less fat, making them a better choice for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide starch that supplies steady energy and helps maintain blood‑sugar levels when eaten in moderation.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Puffed potatoes retain some vitamin C, an antioxidant that supports the immune system.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potassium aids normal muscle and nerve function and helps regulate fluid balance.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: The product contains no gluten, making it safe for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some flavored varieties are high in salt, which may be a concern for individuals with hypertension.

items.title: Allergens in seasonings
items.content: Flavor additives can contain dairy or soy ingredients that may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high GI, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Possible preservatives
items.content: To extend shelf life, anti‑oxidants may be used, which are not suitable for all consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Popped chips are convenient as a standalone snack, tossed into salads for crunch, served with dips, or used in recipes as a lighter alternative to traditional fried chips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the chips in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, transfer to an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption and loss of crispness.
